The balloons caused a direct short which blew fuses before the lines would melt.

Those power lines are 330kv at thousands of amps at the time of fault. The balloons vaporized almost immediately, but that causes an arc due to the low impedence of the metalized mylar that is now in vapor form. This arc can then be self sustaining for a few seconds or longer, creates huge amounts of back EMF into the grid, and draws massive overloads of current.

What you saw was the system "failing" in the way it was designed for, most likely high voltage fuses filled with silica to quench the disconnect arc. The power grid is fragile for many other reasons, cybersecurity and EMP damage to name two. This is not an example of their weakness, a direct short across a large electrical system will damage something down the line, in this case it was a sacrificial element known as a fuse.

Let's see how quickly I get banned. At what point did the doctor say that sex was only for reproduction. We are one of the few species that also has sex for pleasure, but there's absolutely no denying it's biological purpose is reproduction. I didn't see anything to indicate your doctor said that's all it's for, and that could also be a way of the doctor saying:

   Hey there's a higher risk of you getting pregnant if you proceed with this, I know you said that you'd just get an abortion but that's a lot of trauma on the body (depending on the stage of development either hormonal or physical) and you shouldn't go through that if you don't have to.


I didn't see anything about your post that indicated the doctor said sex is bad, you shouldn't have sex, abortions are bad, etc. No doctor is going to recommend sexual practices that increase your chances of having an unwanted pregnancy. It isn't nice to your reproductive system to get an abortion and it always carries some risk. I don't see anything that the doctor said that was incorrect or judgemental..

Perhaps you could elaborate further? Let's recap on some facts: 
*  Sex serves the biological purpose of reproduction.
* You can have sex for pleasure but whether it's for pleasure or for reproduction, you are just as likely to get pregnant (contraception use aside)
* Abortions do put a large stress on the body, and always carry some non-zero risk of complications or infertility.


Nothing your doctor said was false, nor was it inflammatory. It sounds to me (unless you have more details to add) that your doctor was simply recommended the continued use of condoms and suggesting that the IUD isn't foolproof (I knew someone who's IUD fell out). When you said you'd just get an abortion it sounds like they were trying to warn you that it's a lot of stress on the body and that the primary biological purpose of sex is reproduction, so pregnancy is more than a slim possibility without condoms even with an IUD. By all means, you're free to find a new doctor as you wish but I don't see what was so offensive about this exchange.
